item.verbatim_text: Data Catalog Vocabulary - United States. The federal metadata standard that data.gov requires for all published datasets. DCAT-US defines which metadata fields are required (such as title, description, modified date, and keywords) and what formats are acceptable for each field. Harvest validation errors occur when dataset metadata does not conform to the DCAT-US schema.
item.grounding_span: Data Catalog Vocabulary - United States. The federal metadata standard that data.gov requires for all published datasets. DCAT-US defines which metadata fields are required (such as title, description, modified date, and keywords) and what formats are acceptable for each field. Harvest validation errors occur when dataset metadata does not conform to the DCAT-US schema.

item.verbatim_text: A dataset is an organized collection of data. The most basic representation of a dataset is data elements presented in tabular form. Each column represents a particular variable. Each row corresponds to a given value of that column’s variable. A dataset may also present information in a variety of non-tabular formats, such as an extensible mark-up language (XML) file, a geospatial data file, or an image file, etc.

item.verbatim_text: The international standard for representing dates and times. ISO 8601 requires dates to be formatted as YYYY-MM-DD with hyphens separating year, month, and day (for example, 2024-03-15). Date format errors are the most common type of harvest validation failure, typically occurring when dates are malformed such as having the year and month run together (201603-01 instead of 2016-03-01).
item.grounding_span: The international standard for representing dates and times. ISO 8601 requires dates to be formatted as YYYY-MM-DD with hyphens separating year, month, and day (for example, 2024-03-15).

item.verbatim_text: An international standard for geospatial metadata. Some federal agencies publish their dataset metadata in ISO 19115 or ISO 19115-2 format. When harvesting these sources, the system converts the ISO metadata into DCAT-US format. Transformation errors can occur if the ISO records are missing required elements that are needed for the conversion.
item.grounding_span: An international standard for geospatial metadata. Some federal agencies publish their dataset metadata in ISO 19115 or ISO 19115-2 format.

item.verbatim_text: A DCAT-US metadata field describing how often a dataset is updated. Must use ISO 8601 duration codes in repeating interval format (such as R/P1W for weekly, R/P1M for monthly, R/P1Y for annual) or the literal value 'irregular' for datasets that are no longer updated. Plain English descriptions like 'Weekly' or 'Monthly' are not accepted and cause validation failures.
item.grounding_span: A DCAT-US metadata field describing how often a dataset is updated. Must use ISO 8601 duration codes in repeating interval format (such as R/P1W for weekly, R/P1M for monthly, R/P1Y for annual) or the literal value 'irregular' for datasets that are no longer updated.

item.verbatim_text: A required DCAT-US metadata field containing the email address for the dataset contact. Must be formatted as a single mailto: URI (for example, mailto:contact@agency.gov) with no extra text, no subject lines, no multiple addresses, and no trailing spaces. Common validation failures include appended subject lines, multiple email addresses in one field, or invisible Unicode characters from copy-pasting.
item.grounding_span: A required DCAT-US metadata field containing the email address for the dataset contact. Must be formatted as a single mailto: URI (for example, mailto:contact@agency.gov) with no extra text, no subject lines, no multiple addresses, and no trailing spaces.

item.verbatim_text: A required DCAT-US metadata field containing tags that describe the dataset's subject matter to help users find it in search results. Must be formatted as an array of strings, even if there is only one keyword (for example, ['environment'] not 'environment'). Datasets must have at least one keyword. Both missing keywords and improperly formatted keyword fields cause validation failures.
item.grounding_span: A required DCAT-US metadata field containing tags that describe the dataset's subject matter to help users find it in search results. Must be formatted as an array of strings, even if there is only one keyword (for example, ['environment'] not 'environment').

item.verbatim_text: A DCAT-US metadata field that must contain a URL pointing to the dataset's license document. The field only accepts valid URIs, not plain text descriptions. For most U.S. government public domain datasets, the correct value is https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/. Text values like 'Public Domain' or 'None' cause validation failures.
item.grounding_span: A DCAT-US metadata field that must contain a URL pointing to the dataset's license document. The field only accepts valid URIs, not plain text descriptions.

item.verbatim_text: A required DCAT-US metadata field containing the date a dataset or its metadata was last updated. Must be formatted in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). The most common harvest error is a malformed modified date where the year and month run together without the required hyphen separator. Missing modified dates also trigger validation failures since this is a required field.
item.grounding_span: A required DCAT-US metadata field containing the date a dataset or its metadata was last updated. Must be formatted in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

item.verbatim_text: An optional DCAT-US metadata field containing the date a dataset was first published or released. When present, must be formatted in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Like the modified field, issued dates commonly fail validation when the year and month are run together without proper hyphen separators.
item.grounding_span: An optional DCAT-US metadata field containing the date a dataset was first published or released. When present, must be formatted in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD).

item.verbatim_text: A harvest error that occurs when a metadata field value does not conform to the DCAT-US schema requirements. The harvester can read the record, but a specific field value is formatted incorrectly, contains an unacceptable value, or is missing when required. Validation errors make up approximately 66% of all harvest failures. These errors typically begin with a field name such as '$.modified' or '$.accrualPeriodicity'.
item.grounding_span: A harvest error that occurs when a metadata field value does not conform to the DCAT-US schema requirements. The harvester can read the record, but a specific field value is formatted incorrectly, contains an unacceptable value, or is missing when required.

item.verbatim_text: A harvest error that occurs before validation when the harvester cannot read or convert a metadata record at all. These indicate structural problems with the source file itself, such as malformed XML, missing required elements in ISO 19115 records, or unrecognizable record structures. Transformation errors make up approximately 32% of harvest failures and always begin with the phrase 'record failed to transform'.
